compound_ladder.label: calibrated (0.21% of lap time)
compound_ladder.derivation: fresh-tyre step prior 0.174 s (calibrated (0.21% of lap time)). The races identify the *net* cost of one step harder over a whole stint, holding stint length and race phase fixed: Monza 2023 +0.188 +/- 0.145 s; Monza 2024 -0.063 +/- 0.126 s; Monza 2025 -0.075 +/- 0.402 s [not used: standard error 0.402 s > 0.15 s (pre-2026 measurement, too imprecise to pool)]; australia-2026 +0.317 +/- 0.345 s; japan-2026 -0.069 +/- 0.664 s; barcelona-2026 +0.060 +/- 0.336 s; austria-2026 +0.106 +/- 0.295 s; belgium-2026 +0.075 +/- 0.323 s; hungary-2026 -0.010 +/- 0.327 s -> pooled +0.056 +/- 0.092 s per step. The model's fresh-tyre offsets are calibrated so that, with its own degradation ladder, it reproduces this net at the stint length it recommends.

regime.derivation: race/practice degradation ratio, stint-fixed-effects estimator on both sessions; residuals pooled with the median: australia-2026 0.75x, japan-2026 0.73x, barcelona-2026 0.70x, austria-2026 0.58x, belgium-2026 0.32x, hungary-2026 0.64x -> management residual 0.67x (spread 0.26 ln); no temperature term (no race-day forecast supplied: no temperature term); the pool gives 0.67x; Monza's own practice->race ratio in [2023, 2024] is 0.49x (+/-0.95 ln), which carries 7% of the precision, so 0.65x applies; the old pooled geometric mean would have given 0.60x. italy-2026's own race is never used
